newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Uncertainty clouds Burton break-up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Uncertainty clouds Burton break-up.

text.p: British retailer Burton Group Plc's plan to float off its Debenhams department stores was described as a sensible move by retail analysts on Tuesday but they were less upbeat on the prospects for its fashion stores standing alone.

The demerger will create two separate retail groups. Debenhams, the highly profitable department store business, and the struggling fashion multiples, including Principles, Top Shop and Dorothy Perkins. The Burton Group name will disappear.

Finance director Andrew Higginson estimated Debenhams could be worth about 1.6 billion pounds ($2.7 billion) and said the valuation of the combined group had been "averaged down" because Debenhams and the fashion stores were at different stages.

"Part of the problem for shareholders was that because the two businesses were at different stages in the recovery cycle...it was difficult to work out which business you were actually buying," he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
The demerger and listing of Debenhams would allow investors to decide whether to choose the successful department store business or the multiples which had a recovery potential within them, he said.
Retail analysts agreed the separation would free Debenhams from the problems dogging the multiples division, which is still struggling to deliver growth from all of its five brands.
"I think what they are doing is right," said Rowan Morgan, retail analyst at Nikko Europe. "Debenhams free of the multiples business will be treated on its own merits."
Analysts estimated Debenhams could be worth between 1.3 and 1.6 billion pounds, with the multiples valued between 550 and 700 million.
They welcomed plans to streamline management at the five multiples business, which they said could bring in cost savings of between 10 to 15 million pounds on an annualised basis.
But they said the fashion multiples' accident prone record made it a much less attractive proposition and warned that separation could focus the spotlight even more closely on its weaknesses.

Burton, the second biggest clothing retailer in Britain after Marks and Spencer Plc, said the demerger would "significantly enhance" shareholder value and was in the best interests of the group's shareholders and customers.
News of the break-up boosted the retailer's shares, which closed 10.5 pence higher at 125.25 pence.
Chief executive John Hoerner, who will head the multiples business after the demerger, said the fashion chains had a long way to go before becoming a true growth business but had great potential.
"Multiples, quite frankly is a good business," he told Reuters in an interview. "But it has got a long way to go. So I would have to say that it is still a little bit of a recovery business."
But Hoerner said that he hoped to see a "real difference" in the performance of the fashion stores business when they begin trading under the new structure next spring.

Having been credited with masterminding Burton's dramatic turnaround from troubles in the British recession of the early 1990s, Hoerner said after working on Debenhams for 10 years it was a world class store.
Asked how long it would take to rev up the group's other businesses, Hoerner said: "I've been working on multiples for five years. I hope it isn't going to take another five."
Burton has successfully rebuilt gross profit margins and revamped its womenswear chains to boost profits.

But persistent problems with its Burton Menswear chain and investors' concerns that the recovery was running out of steam have dogged the shares in recent months. On Monday the shares had sunk to 112.5 pence, their lowest for a year.
The group's first half profits published in May were up 23 percent, but the sales performance from the multiples was not perky enough to reassure investors.

Debenhams, which has around 92 stores in Britain, made profits of 102.8 million pounds ($173 million) in the year to August 1996, a 21 percent increase on the previous 12 months. ($ = 0.594 British Pounds)
